result.reasoning:
REFUTED — the arithmetic reproduces exactly, but the premise the finding rests on is fabricated, and the kernel's output is correct under the only median definition this codebase has.

(1) The numbers all reproduce. `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute_madz_median/r1_repro.py`: `ops_ext.in_madz(torch.tensor([[[nan,nan,nan,1.,2.,3.,4.]]]), 4)[0,0,6] == 1.3489797115325928`, which is the lower-median value (med=2.0, MAD=1.0); textbook would be 1.0117344332. The d=10 heavy-ties window returns NaN (lower-median MAD=0) where textbook gives MAD=0.0811. The parity pattern reproduces too (r3): at odd d=15, 0 differing cells and book overlap 1.000000; at even d, large differences.

(2) The premise is false. The finding asserts "in_madz's docstring defines median_d/MAD_d as the ordinary statistical median (average the two middle values ...)". The docstring, printed verbatim in r4, says only ``median_d`` and ``MAD_d`` — it states no tie rule. `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md:39` likewise says only "近 d 分钟中位数". The reporter wrote "a from-scratch numpy reference built only from the docstring", silently injected `np.median`'s tie rule into it, and then reported the kernel as wrong against their own invention.

(3) The codebase resolves the ambiguity the other way, unanimously. `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:11` states the conventions are "the same as AlphaCube's kernels", and every median in AlphaCube is `torch.nanmedian` (lower median). Measured in r4 on [1,2,3,4], all return 2.0, not 2.5: `in_med(x,4)` (the rolling minute median over the *same* window — AlphaCube/src/alphacube/operators/dt_in.py:384), `in_median`, `day_median`, `cs_median`, `common._median` (common.py:396), `common.nanmedian_last` (common.py:456). `cross_madz` (ops_ext.py:646, the day-axis sibling carrying a word-for-word identical formula in its docstring) uses `torch.nanmedian` as well. The reporter cites `alphacube/mining/scoring.py:138` as proof this is "a known footgun ... that simply wasn't re-checked"; read in place, that line does the opposite — it *documents the lower median as the house meaning of median* ("distinct 用的是 torch.median(偶数天时取中间两个里小的那个)"). So in_madz implements its library's documented median. No contract is broken; nothing is silent.

(4) The "false NaN" limb is not a contract break either. The docstring's operative clause is "(MAD = 0)" and the code gates on exactly `mad > 0`. Verified over 20,000 random windows with no counterexamples (r5): under the lower median, MAD == 0 ⟺ at least ⌈d/2⌉ of the d minutes sit on exactly one value; textbook's threshold is ⌊d/2⌋+1. The two stillness cutoffs differ by exactly one minute (≥half vs >half). The reporter's "perfectly normal, non-flat window" has 5 of its 10 values at exactly −1.0501 — half the window pinned to one price, i.e. precisely the stale/locked-quote state this op declines to score on A-share minute data. Which of ≥half / >half is the better cutoff is a judgment call, not a defect. Only the English gloss "the window does not move at all" is loose for even d, which is docstring wording and changes no number.

(5) Applying the suggested fix would be a regression. `torch.nanquantile(w, 0.5)` would make in_madz's internal median disagree with `in_med(x, d)` — the same library's rolling minute median over the identical window (r4: in_med → 2.0, nanquantile → 2.5) — creating a real inconsistency where none exists, and splitting in_madz from cross_madz. It is also ~1.6x slower and sort-based, so it needs a full extra copy of the window tensor (r2: 0.521s vs 0.344s on (8000,241,30)); engine.py:124-132 with kernels.py:211-217 hands an `in_*` kernel (chunk_symbols*n_days, 241) rows — 52,434 × 241 × 30 = 379M-element windows at the default 2 GiB chunk budget, so that is ~1.5 GB of extra sort buffer per call. (The 2^24 numel ceiling the older PyTorch quantile had is gone in torch 2.14, so that part is not an obstacle.)

(6) Most importantly, the finding's own materiality argument cuts against changing anything. On a realistic A-share-like panel (600 stocks × 60 days × 241 minutes, 0.01 tick grid, stale quotes, limit locks, missing minutes), r3 measured the switch against the project's actual selection rule (daily top-10% equal weight): top-10% book overlap 0.725 for F108's `day_max(abs_(in_madz(Close,30)))` — the only madz variant that actually scored (ut +5.2%) — 0.249 for F102's `day_kurt(in_madz(Ret,10))`, 0.575 for F104's `day_quantile_q25(in_madz(Amt,30))`, 0.403 for F105's `day_mean(abs_(in_madz(Amt,30)))`, and 1.000 at odd d. Every recorded F102/F104/F105/F108 verdict involving in_madz was produced under the current, library-consistent definition. Swapping the tie rule would silently invalidate them. That makes this a redefinition decision for the user, requiring a re-run — not a bug fix.

No test anywhere in Partura or AlphaCube pins in_madz to a textbook-median reference (grep for "madz" in both tests/ trees: no hits), so there is no second source of truth that the kernel contradicts.

result.corrected_fix:
Do NOT apply the suggested kernel change. There is no defect to fix: `median` in this codebase means `torch.nanmedian` (lower of the two middle values on an even count) in every single operator — `in_med`, `in_median`, `day_median`, `cs_median`, `common._median`, `common.nanmedian_last`, and `cross_madz`, in_madz's own day-axis sibling with an identical docstring formula — and `alphacube/mining/scoring.py:138` documents that convention in writing. Swapping only in_madz to `torch.nanquantile` would make it disagree with `in_med(x, d)` over the very same window, which is a new inconsistency, and would silently invalidate the recorded F102/F104/F105/F108 verdicts (measured: top-10% book moves 27%-75% at the even d those studies used, 0% at odd d).

The only thing worth touching is the docstring, and only if the user wants the ambiguity closed — a no-op on every number:
1. `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:381` — spell out the tie rule, e.g. "median_d / MAD_d use torch.nanmedian (the lower of the two middle values on an even count), as every other median in the library does".
2. `/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:382-383` — replace the loose gloss "where the window does not move at all (MAD = 0)" with what MAD = 0 provably means under that convention (verified, 0 counterexamples in 20,000 windows): "where at least ceil(d/2) of the d minutes hold exactly one value (MAD = 0)". Same edit applies to `cross_madz` at ops_ext.py:648.
If instead the user decides they actually want the mid-average median as the definition, that is a redefinition, not a fix: it must change in_madz AND cross_madz AND (for consistency) the library's other medians together, and F102/F104/F105/F108 must be re-run before their recorded numbers are quoted again.
